hypotheses.statement: Each actuated joint can sustain a torque of at most its declared capacity in each direction; torques beyond capacity are excluded from the feasible set.
hypotheses.source_note: Capacities are a population prior; values and sources arrive with NSX-04.

hypotheses.statement: Contact loads lie inside a friction cone with a declared coefficient, approximated by a polyhedron with a declared facet count and error bound.
Each hand keeps at least a declared axial squeeze on the club, so hand contact never goes slack.
hypotheses.source_note: Preload magnitudes are not sourced here; Choi and Park 2020 measured internal grip forces but no value is adopted.

conventions.statement: Closure rows and hand wrenches are expressed in the grip frame: origin at the midpoint of the two grip points, u along the shaft toward the clubhead, v the face-normal projection orthogonal to u, w = u x v.
Forces are scaled by a characteristic force and moments by a characteristic moment before rank decisions and in null-space coordinates.
Numerical rank uses a relative singular-value tolerance against the largest singular value of the scaled matrix.

non_claims: Static per-frame feasible sets over-approximate trajectory-feasible ranges.
FAMILY_DEPENDENT quantities are conditional on the declared hypotheses; torque capacities are priors, not measurements.
An allocation is a hypothesis-conditioned representative of the admissible family, not an estimate of the true hand loads or joint torques.
Refused, rejected and infeasible frames are reported as such and are never repaired or given a relaxed tolerance.
Restriction sensitivity is not computed by this contract version.
